hero.title: Map the future of work: country by country, skill by skill
hero.sub: Personalized insights built using real World Bank data and clear, transparent calculations that can be checked and trusted

about.title: What can you do with MAPPED?
about.sub: Mapped helps you understand how AI is reshaping jobs across different countries and skill levels. Explore how roles are classified, how exposure is calculated, and how local economic conditions change the impact of automation.
about.card1Desc: Global job automation estimates using real country data and show the results as clear risk levels on an interactive map using Frey-Osborne baselines
about.card2Desc: Five-question aptitude tests mapped to ISCO-08 + ESCO produce a tiered AI-resilience score, a Grow plan of UN SDG community projects and personalized opportunity matches against locally calibrated occupations
about.card3Desc: Searchable, anonymized talent pool for ministries and employers, filterable by aptitude tier, ISCO group, and AI-resilience band, with deterministic top-skill rankings exported to CSV
about.card4Desc: Leverage World Bank data on jobs and income, with backups when needed, and include full details on where the data comes from and how it's calculated

how.title: A reliable calibration pipeline
how.sub: Every calibrated risk number on the platform follows the same four-factor formula. You can audit it row-by-row, including the World Bank source year and indicator code.
how.step1Desc: Frey-Osborne US automation probability for the ISCO major group, employment-weighted
how.step2Desc: Country structural multiplier reflecting labor-market context
how.formula: = baseline automation risk × country adjustment × informal economy adjustment × wage adjustment

evidence.desc1: Pulls unregistered employment rate (SL.ISV.IFRM.ZS) and GDP per capita data (NY.GDP.PCAP.CD) per country, with explicit fallback when WDI hasn't refreshed.
evidence.desc2: Each risk shows the [low–high] uncertainty interval, the band thresholds it crosses, and the resulting confidence.
evidence.desc3: CSV exports include calibration provenance: country, year mode, source years, and live-vs-fallback data
